lens: Figma/whiteboard canvas: scenarios and personas built visually as nodes on an infinite canvas
name: Call Canvas
one_liner: A dark, spatial studio where personas, talk tracks and rubrics are nodes you wire into a call, with a live coach rail while you talk and an evidence-linked replay afterward.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: personas and scenarios live as nodes on an infinite canvas, and the AI wizard is a wired graph (sources feed a Persona Synth node that emits Persona, Scenario and Rubric nodes). Changed: the canvas is the build and browse surface only. Live call and debrief use fixed, glanceable layouts, because the Mobbin live-call references (Dialpad, Fireflies, Grain) and phone use need stable panels, not free-form space. Self-scores (1-10): A 8, B 7, C 8, D 6.5, E 6.5, F1 6, F2 6, F3 3 (F3 at 3 means leaning toward worth building).

palette.use: App background under a 24px dot grid (light: #F6F7F9)
Primary action, live recording, on-track state (light: #0F766E)

design_language.typography: Geist for UI (500 body and controls, 600 headings, -0.02em tracking on display). Geist Mono for timers, scores, timecodes and rubric weights, with tabular numerals wherever a number moves. Landing display 56/60, page titles 28/34, body 15/22, meta 12/16. No serif accents, no gradient text.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radii 14px cards, 10px controls, pill chips. Depth comes from surface steps (canvas, surface, raised) and 1px hairlines with a faint inner top highlight, not drop shadows. Live states get a 1px signal ring and a 24px glow at 16% opacity. The coach cue uses a violet ring, never the signal colour, so the rep can tell advice from status.
design_language.motion: Panels and sheets 200ms ease-out. Cue cards spring in from the right (stiffness 320, damping 30) and hold a 2-second violet ring pulse. Score dial sweeps 900ms on debrief. Wizard wires draw in 400ms as a source connects. Only the voice orb loops; every motion falls back to an opacity fade under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.5px stroke: 16px in chips, 20px in navigation. Custom 20px duotone glyphs for the four node types (source, persona, scenario, rubric). The OpenAI engine appears as a plain text chip (Realtime, gpt-4.1-mini), never a logo, so it does not imply endorsement.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default on :root; light tokens apply under prefers-color-scheme: light and a data-theme attribute override from the header toggle. Light is a full mode, not an afterthought. Body text pairs meet WCAG AA in both modes; the dot grid drops to 4% opacity in light mode.

navigation_and_ia: A 64px left icon rail (Practice, Library, Create, Progress, Team, Settings) that expands on hover. Cmd-K runs any action. Practice is the home canvas with recent calls and nodes. Library and Create share one canvas in two modes. Team appears only inside an org. Mobile uses a bottom bar (Practice, Library, Create, Progress, More). Call and debrief routes are full-bleed with no rail, so the call owns the screen.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Architecture: the persona model never sees coaching. A separate OpenAI evaluator (gpt-4.1-mini, structured output) reads each turn against the active rubric and emits cue deltas. Cue types: whisper (next best question), objection alert (type plus an acknowledge-then-anchor line), talk-track progress, pace (talk ratio), and rubric delta with an evidence pin. Live numbers are labelled 'live estimate' and settle into the graded score at the end. Target: a cue within 2 seconds of the rep's turn in text mode and 3 seconds in voice. Each cue has Why and helpful or not buttons that feed prompt tuning. Self-rating D: 6.5, above the 5.0 baseline only if the evaluator meets latency; if coaching is post-call only, D falls below baseline.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: about 140 packs at launch, roughly seven per industry across 20 industries, covering SDR, AE, CSM, collections, recruiting and the rest. Each pack has three difficulty levels and tagged objection types, stored as versioned JSON validated by zod and CI. Contributors add a pack as a file and see it on the board before merging. Wizard: sources in, one Persona Synth call returns Persona, Scenario and Rubric as structured outputs; each field cites its source sentence, and manual edits survive regenerate. Self-rating E: 6.5. Pack count and objection quality, not UI, are the constraint, so ship 40 reviewed packs before claiming 140.
signature_moments: A violet whisper card lands in the rail the moment a prospect says 'send me an email', with one line of what to say.
Clicking any quote in the debrief scrubs the replay to that second.
Wizard wires draw in as sources connect, and each generated field shows the sentence it came from.
The score dial sweeps while the live rubric numbers settle into the final grade.
The landing hero replays real product output rather than a stock illustration.
On mobile, the cue pill docks above the composer and expands into evidence on tap.
openai_fund_angle: Make OpenAI the visible engine, not a logo. A model rail under the top bar names the model for each job: Realtime for voice, gpt-4.1-mini for live cues and grading, structured-output synthesis for the wizard. A per-call cost chip shows cents from real token usage. Self-hosters paste their own key and see spend in Settings. Contributors get 'Add a persona pack' and 'Fix a rubric' buttons that open prefilled issues, plus a CONTRIBUTING guide and AGENTS.md so maintainers can use Codex CLI for pack generation and PR review, the maintenance workflow the Codex for Open Source program targets (https://openai.com/form/codex-for-oss/). The brief's $25K credit figure was not verified in this run.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (about 2 weeks, estimate): add Tailwind v4 and token CSS behind a theme flag, install shadcn primitives, rebuild landing, pre-call and debrief on the new tokens, keep old routes live. Phase 2 (about 2 weeks): live coach rail with a separate evaluator endpoint behind a flag, with the current chat view as fallback. Phase 3: library grid and board, a JSON pack format that migrates the three built-ins and the localStorage scenarios, 40 reviewed packs, then the wizard. Phase 4: progress and manager views, growing to about 140 packs. Lazy-load React Flow and the wizard routes.

risks: The canvas metaphor can read as a diagram tool; keep the grid as the default library view and make the canvas opt-in.
Latency: a second evaluator call per turn adds cost and delay. If p95 cue latency exceeds 3 seconds, coaching becomes post-call and D drops below baseline.
Pack quality is the bottleneck: generated objections need human review, so claim the pack count only after review.
A dark-first canvas can hurt print and low-contrast displays; light mode must be tested as a first-class theme.
React Flow and motion add bundle weight; lazy-load both and measure the landing bundle.
Hyperbound and Second Nature are funded and more polished; the pitch is open source, self-hostable and bring-your-own OpenAI key, not feature parity.
Research caveat: Firecrawl hit rate limits on most attempts, so competitor and OpenAI-program claims rest on search excerpts, not full page scrapes. Verify before citing.
